final_json.causal_explanation: The database stores its data files under /var/lib. When the filesystem containing /var/lib reaches 100% capacity, the OS returns ENOSPC (No space left on device) for write operations. The database engine cannot allocate or extend data files, WAL/redo logs, or temporary files, so all write transactions fail. This directly matches the reported symptom of DB write failures.
remediation_steps: Identify the largest consumers under /var/lib (e.g., du -xh --max-depth=2 /var/lib | sort -rh | head) to pinpoint the offending directory (commonly /var/lib/<db> data/WAL files, /var/lib/docker, /var/lib/journal, /var/lib/apt, /var/lib/mysql, etc.).
Free space safely: rotate/truncate or archive old database WAL/redo logs if the DB supports online log management; remove old rotated logs, core dumps, and package caches (apt/yum) under /var/lib.
If the DB is the primary consumer, perform an online checkpoint/compaction or move data to a larger volume, then resize or add storage to the /var/lib mount.
After freeing space, verify with df -h /var/lib that usage is below ~85%, then restart or re-enable the DB service and confirm writes succeed.
Add monitoring/alerting on filesystem usage (e.g., alert at 80%) and enable log rotation to prevent recurrence.

Removing files under /var/lib may break other services that depend on them (e.g., package manager state, systemd journal, container storage).
If the DB is already in a failed state, forcing writes after partial failure may require recovery/repair (e.g., crash recovery, fsck) before normal operation resumes.
Adding storage or resizing the volume may require downtime depending on the filesystem and hypervisor.
